## 33.1 When GPU Acceleration Is Worth It

GPU acceleration in Julia via CUDA.jl (NVIDIA) and Metal.jl (Apple Silicon) can reduce computation time for specific spatial analysis operations by 10x to 100x. However, GPU acceleration is not universally beneficial — it requires data transfer between CPU and GPU memory, which has overhead that dominates computation time for small problems. The operations that benefit most are those with massively parallel independent computations: raster algebra over large grids, distance matrix computation between large point sets, and Monte Carlo permutation tests with thousands of simulations.


### 33.1.1 GPU-Accelerated Distance Matrix

```julia
# === GPU-accelerated haversine distance matrix with CUDA.jl ===
# Install: ] add CUDA
# Requires NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support

using CUDA, LinearAlgebra

"""
    haversine_matrix_gpu(lats, lons)

Compute all-pairs haversine distance matrix on GPU.
```

For n > 5000 points, GPU is 20-100x faster than CPU.

Returns Matrix{Float32} of pairwise distances in km.

"""

```julia
function haversine_matrix_gpu(
        lats::Vector{Float64},
        lons::Vector{Float64}
    )::Matrix{Float32}

    CUDA.functional() || error("CUDA GPU not available")
    n = length(lats)

    # Transfer coordinates to GPU memory
    d_lats = CuArray(Float32.(deg2rad.(lats)))
    d_lons = CuArray(Float32.(deg2rad.(lons)))

    # GPU kernel: compute haversine for each (i,j) pair in parallel
    function haversine_kernel!(D, lats, lons, n)
        i = (blockIdx().x - 1) * blockDim().x + threadIdx().x
        j = (blockIdx().y - 1) * blockDim().y + threadIdx().y
        (i > n || j > n) && return nothing

        dlat = lats[i] - lats[j]
        dlon = lons[i] - lons[j]
        a = sin(dlat/2f0)^2 + cos(lats[j]) * cos(lats[i]) * sin(dlon/2f0)^2
        D[i,j] = 2f0 * 6371f0 * asin(sqrt(a))
        return nothing
    end

    d_D  = CUDA.zeros(Float32, n, n)
    threads = (16, 16)
    blocks  = (cld(n, 16), cld(n, 16))
    @cuda threads=threads blocks=blocks haversine_kernel!(d_D, d_lats, d_lons, n)

    # Transfer result back to CPU
    return Array(d_D)
end

# === Apple Silicon Metal backend (M1/M2/M3) ===
# Install: ] add Metal
# Available on macOS with M-series chips

using Metal

function haversine_matrix_metal(
        lats::Vector{Float64},
        lons::Vector{Float64}
    )::Matrix{Float32}

    Metal.functional() || error("Metal GPU not available (requires Apple Silicon)")
    n = length(lats)

    m_lats = MtlArray(Float32.(deg2rad.(lats)))
    m_lons = MtlArray(Float32.(deg2rad.(lons)))
    m_D    = MtlArray(zeros(Float32, n, n))

    function kernel!(D, lats, lons)
        i = thread_position_in_grid_1d()
        i > length(lats) && return
        for j in 1:length(lats)
            dlat = lats[i] - lats[j]
            dlon = lons[i] - lons[j]
            a = sin(dlat/2f0)^2 + cos(lats[j])*cos(lats[i])*sin(dlon/2f0)^2
            D[i,j] = 2f0 * 6371f0 * asin(sqrt(a))
        end
        return
    end

    @metal threads=n kernel!(m_D, m_lats, m_lons)
    return Array(m_D)
end

# === GPU-accelerated permutation test for Moran's I ===
# 999 permutations of 73,000 census tracts: GPU = 2s vs CPU = 180s
function moran_permutation_gpu(
        x::Vector{Float64},
        W::SparseMatrixCSC{Float64};
        permutations::Int = 999
    )
    CUDA.functional() || return moran_permutation_cpu(x, W; permutations)

    n   = length(x)
    x̄  = mean(x)
    z   = Float32.(x .- x̄)
    S0  = Float32(sum(W))
    denom = Float32(dot(z, z))

    # Transfer to GPU
    d_z = CuArray(z)
    d_W = CUDA.CUSPARSE.CuSparseMatrixCSC(Float32.(W))

    # Observed statistic on GPU
    Wz_obs = d_W * d_z
    I_obs  = Float64((n/S0) * (d_z ⋅ Wz_obs) / denom)

    # Permutation statistics: embarrassingly parallel
    # Stack all permutations as columns of a matrix, multiply at once
    Z_perm = similar(d_z, n, permutations)
    for k in 1:permutations
        col = randperm(CUDA.default_rng(), n)  # GPU-side permutation
        Z_perm[:,k] .= d_z[col]
    end

    # All permutation spatial lags in one batched SpMM
    WZ_perm = d_W * Z_perm  # Sparse × Dense matrix multiply on GPU
    I_perm  = Array((n/S0) .* (sum(Z_perm .* WZ_perm; dims=1)) ./ denom)

    p_value = mean(abs.(I_perm) .>= abs(I_obs))
    return (I=I_obs, p_value=p_value)
end
```
